Rashi on Temurah 7a:11:1.english: That has anything too long - That one of its limbs was broken.

Rashi on Temurah 7a:11:2.english: Uncloven - [An animal] whose hooves are uncloven.

Rashi on Temurah 7a:11:3.hebrew: כתובין בפרשה - ועלייהו כתיב ״לא תקריבו״, ודרשינן: ״לא תקדישו״:
Rashi on Temurah 7a:11:3.english: [They] are written in the passage - And concerning them it is written: “You shall not offer,” and we expound: “You shall not consecrate.”

Rashi on Temurah 7a:12:1.hebrew: שמא לא שנינו - שיהא חייב משום הקדשה אלא בתמורה, לפי שהתמורה חלה על בעל מום קבוע וקדוש קדושה גמורה, שאינה יוצאה לחולין ליגזז וליעבד אפילו על ידי פדיון, אלא הויא כשאר קדשים שקדם הקדשן את מומן. והך משנה לקמן בפרק שני (תמורה דף טז:), כדכתיב: ״טוב ברע או רע בטוב ואם המר ימיר וגו'״. והואיל וקדושה גמורה היא, לוקה עליה אם המיר והביא בעלת מום שיקדיש ותפסה בתמורת בהמת קודש תמימה. אבל הקדיש בעל מום מעיקרא, לא אמינא דלילקי, דדיקלא בעלמא הוא, אלא אם כן הקריבו:
Rashi on Temurah 7a:12:1.english: Perhaps we did not learn - That one is liable on account of consecration, except in [the case of] substitution; because substitution takes effect upon [an animal with] a permanent blemish, and it becomes sanctified with complete sanctity, which does not go out to non-sacred status to be shorn or to be worked even by means of redemption, but rather it is like other consecrated [animals] whose consecration preceded their blemish. And this mishna is later in the second chapter (Temurah 16b), as it is written: “Good for bad, or bad for good; and if he shall at all substitute...” (Leviticus 27:10). And since it is complete sanctity, one is flogged for it if he substituted and brought a blemished [animal] to consecrate, and it took hold as the substitution for an unblemished consecrated animal. But [if] one consecrated [an animal that was] blemished from the outset, I would not say that he should be flogged, for it is merely [like consecrating] a date palm, unless he sacrificed it.

Rashi on Temurah 7a:13:1.english: They were counted and concluded - This implies that they were precise and did not find more [than five]. And if it were so that [the statement] is speaking of [consecration] through substitution:

Rashi on Temurah 7a:13:2.english: There are six, for - There is the prohibition of "He shall not substitute."

Rashi on Temurah 7a:13:3.hebrew: אלא מאי בבעל מום מעיקרו - ועל ידי הקדש, אמאי לקי? הא לא חיילא עליה קדושת מזבח כלל, דדיקלא בעלמא הוא, ולא אקדשיה אלא לדמי:
Rashi on Temurah 7a:13:3.english: Rather, what? [Is it speaking] of [an animal] blemished from the outset - And [if it is] through [direct] consecration, why is he flogged? Behold, the sanctity of the altar does not take effect upon it at all, for it is a mere date palm, and he consecrated it only for [its] monetary value.

Rashi on Temurah 7a:15:1.english: There is none of its type - That is fit for the altar.

Rashi on Temurah 7a:15:2.hebrew: בעל מום איכא במינו - ראוי למזבח. וכיון דאיכא במינו ראוי, איכא בזיון, כיון דשבק מידי דחזי ואקדיש מידי דלא חזי:
Rashi on Temurah 7a:15:2.english: A blemished [animal], there is [an item] of its type - [That is] fit for the altar. And since there is [an item] of its type [that is] fit, there is a disgrace, since he left that which is fit and consecrated that which is not fit.

Rashi on Temurah 7a:16:1.hebrew: אפי' אקדשיה לדמי נסכים - דהשתא ליכא בזיון כל כך, שאין במינו ראוי לנסכים, ועוד דהא לדמי אקדשיה — אפי' הכי לקי:
Rashi on Temurah 7a:16:1.english: Even [if] he consecrated it for the value of libations - For now, there is not so much disgrace, since there is none of its type fit for libations, and furthermore, because he consecrated it [only] for [its] monetary value — even so, he is flogged.

Tosafot on Temurah 7a:16:1.hebrew: אפילו אקדיש לדמי נסכים לקי - וה"ה מקדיש לדמי עולה. והא דאמר לקמן (תמורה דף יח:): המקדיש נקבה לעולה — ימכר ויפלו דמיו לעולה — צ"ל דלקי. וכן הא דתנן פרק כיצד מערימין (לקמן תמורה כז:): אמר על הבהמה טמאה ועל בעלת מום: "הרי אלו עולה" — לא אמר כלום; "הרי אלו לעולה" — ימכרו ויביא בדמיהם עולה — צריך לומר דלקי:
Tosafot on Temurah 7a:16:1.english: "Even [one who] consecrates [it] for the value of libations is flogged" - And the same applies to one who consecrates [it] for the value of a burnt offering. And as for that which [the Gemara] says later (Temurah 18b): "One who consecrates a female [animal] for a burnt offering, it shall be sold and its proceeds shall fall to [i.e., be used for] a burnt offering" — one must say that he is flogged. And similarly, that which we learned in the chapter Keitzad Maarimin (below, Temurah 27b): [If] one said regarding an impure animal or regarding a blemished animal: "These are a burnt offering," he has said nothing; "These are for a burnt offering," they shall be sold and he shall bring a burnt offering with their proceeds — one must say that he is flogged [in the case of the blemished animal].
